newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates end steady, gilt prices rally.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates end steady, gilt prices rally.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed at 1.75-2.00 percent on Friday, unchanged from the day's opening levels, dealers said.
"The call money ruled in the range of 1.50-2.25 percent, while it opened at 2.25 percent and closed at 2.25 percent," Manoj Rane, Associate Vice President at Indusind Bank, said.
Rane said the market was buying short-dated securities, specially 1997 and 1998 maturity paper, as it expected the cut-off yield for Friday's auction to be in the region of 6.75-7.25 percent.
"Volume on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) rose by 18 million on Friday to touch 4.30 billion against the previous day's volume," dealers said.
The security market was very active on Friday across all the maturities, and the prices of securities have risen by 20 basis points for short and medium dated paper, dealers said.

The 13.50 percent 1997 stock rose by 17 paise to 102.57 rupees and 11.75 percent 2001 stock was traded at 94.05 rupees against Thursday's price of 94.88 rupees, while the 13.82 percent 2002 stock was traded at 101.86 rupees compared to the previous day's price of 101.46 rupees, dealers said.

The treasury bills yield fell marginally on Friday, a dealer said. The yield on treasury bills maturing in October 1997 fell by 40-50 basis points to 10.0-10.1 percent compared to Thursday's levels, while the January maturity treasury bill dealt at 7.35 percent, he said.
There were no trades on commercial paper and certificates of deposit on Friday and the inter-corporate deposits were quoted at 18-19.5 percent for P1+ rated companies.
